flags.why: The hypotheses require a countable transitive M ⊆ ZFSet.{u} satisfying pairing, union, power set, separation, collection, infinity and choice, together with K ∈ M that is inaccessible in M. I re-read the de Bruijn encodings of the hypothesis axioms: choice (196-198) through choiceFunctionFormula (85-88) and orderedPairFormula (67-70, Kuratowski pairs matching ZFSet.pair), infinity (192-194) and powerSet (169-172). All read as the standard axioms, so no hypothesis is accidentally contradictory. GroundStandardInaccessible (142-144) reads as 'uncountable regular strong-limit cardinal of M', with groundPower κ = P(κ) ∩ M = P^M(κ). Such an M exists in Lean's intended semantics (ZFC + ω inaccessibles). With inaccessibles κ₀ < κ₁, a countable elementary submodel of V_{κ₁} collapses to a ctm of ZFC + 'κ₀ is inaccessible'. That ctm is hereditarily countable, so it lies in the interpretation of ZFSet.{u}. By soundness Lean cannot refute the hypotheses, so the theorem is not vacuously provable. The extra internal inaccessible is a narrowing, and docs/244.md:11 declares it. It is not a vacuity.

flags.why: All hypotheses can be met at once. (1) A coherator exists. stage 0 can be Θ₀ (Hom S T := ULift (S.realize ⟶ T.realize), base = up). It is initial, because map_base forces every Morphism out of it, and it preserves globular sums, because Shape.attach is realized as the presheaf pushout. Free extensions along admissible pairs and sequential colimits exist among globular theories (an essentially algebraic, locally presentable category). Adjoining all admissible pairs at every stage gives the contractibility conjunct of IsCoherator. (2) Models exist: the constant-PUnit presheaf satisfies the pullback condition, and freeShape / disk are models by construction (lines 343-348). (3) For the remaining hypotheses take X = disk C n, a = 𝟙, Y = disk C (n+1), i = J C n, b = 𝟙. IsPushout 𝟙 J J 𝟙 holds trivially, and disk C n is cellular: the free model on the n-globe is built from the empty initial model by attaching its 2 cells per dimension below n and one n-cell. This instance has content, since it asserts that J is a weak equivalence. Restricting admissible pairs to height ≤ n+1 (line 271) only removes filler obligations. That enlarges the class of coherators and makes the theorem stronger, not vacuous.

flags.why: IsGeodesicOn and IsJacobiFieldOn are the genuine equations. For s ∈ U (open) with γ s ∈ c.source (open), c ∘ γ and the coordinate field are smooth near s (γ is continuous, and fieldCoordinates is ContDiffOn on the open U ∩ γ⁻¹ c.source). The deriv terms and the deriv of alongDerivative at s are therefore genuine. The equations read (c∘γ)'' + Γ((c∘γ)', (c∘γ)') = 0 and D_sD_sJ + R(J, γ')γ' = 0, which is the Jacobi equation for this sign of R. NoConjugatePoints is therefore exactly 'no nontrivial Jacobi field along a geodesic vanishes at two parameters', on every open interval and including constant geodesics (docs/358.md:9). Its premises are satisfiable, e.g. J = γ' or J = (s − a)·γ'. It is not vacuously true for every metric: it fails for any metric containing a region isometric to more than a hemisphere of a round 3-sphere, and every closed 3-manifold carries one because M # S³ ≅ M. So ∃ g, NoConjugatePoints g is a genuine claim.

lean/docs/358.md:9: The formalized result separates absence of conjugate points from nonpositive sectional curvature. It constructs a closed connected orientable smooth three-manifold with a smooth Riemannian metric having no conjugate points, while the same manifold admits no smooth metric of everywhere nonpositive sectional curvature. The no-conjugate-points assertion ranges over all geodesics and tangent-bundle Jacobi fields, including constant geodesics and unbounded time intervals. The separate no-focal-points and CAT(0) consequences are not included.

flags.why: Mathlib's Laplacian on E → F is Σᵢ iteratedFDeriv ℝ 2 u x (bᵢ, bᵢ), using the global iteratedFDeriv. For x ≠ 0, ContDiffOn ℝ 2 u {0}ᶜ on the open set {0}ᶜ gives ContDiffAt ℝ 2 u x, so the global iteratedFDeriv equals the classical second derivative at x. The same holds for v. The rpow terms are also genuine: ‖x‖ > 0 for x ≠ 0, and v x, u x > 0. This flag matters because the theorem is a nonexistence claim. A junk Laplacian (0) would turn equation_u into '0 = positive', which no u satisfies, and ¬∃ would be trivially true. That weakening path is closed.
